I'm 38 years old, I've been farming these lands in Quzhou since I was young, and I know what works here. Around here, the wheat-maize double crop is the bread and butter — nearly every household does it, and for good reason. The soil is fertile, the wells give us water, and the government station buys our grain at a stable price. I'm not going to gamble my family's income on some trendy crop I've never grown before.

This autumn, I'll sow winter wheat on my full 6 mu. I use an improved variety like the ones from the county supply store — yields are consistently over 1000 jin per mu if the weather cooperates. Before sowing, I'll run the rotary tiller to break up the stubble and level the field. For fertilizer, I'll put down compound fertilizer as basal and topdress with urea at green-up and jointing. I know some neighbors over-fertilize, but I've found that about 28 kg of nitrogen, 10 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium per mu gives me a good stand without wasting money. The wheat needs water, especially through the dry spring, so I'll irrigate four times total — including the winter irrigation to protect against frost, then jointing, heading, and grain filling. I'll spray herbicide once before emergence, insecticide twice for aphids and armyworms, and fungicide once if powdery mildew shows up — about four pesticide runs in total. I expect around 1050 kg per mu.

Come early June, as soon as the wheat is harvested, I'll plant summer maize. There's no time to waste — the heat units are tight, so I plant no-tillage directly into the wheat stubble using the seeder. I always buy hybrid seed; the vigor and drought tolerance are worth the extra cost. Maize gets one basal compound application and maybe a side-dressing if the leaves look pale — about 22 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I'll irrigate twice, at the big-flush stage and grain filling. Pests are the main worry — corn borers and armyworms hit hard in July and August, so I'll spray insecticide, herbicide, and fungicide across about four applications. I should get around 1150 kg per mu if the autumn rains don't fail.

This is my plan. It's what my father did, it's what my neighbors do, and it's what puts food on the table.
